title: two propagations in one compound expression compile and run, and the second one never runs after the first fails
notes: RETIRED REFUSAL, kept under its old filename so the COVERAGE.md rows that cite it keep resolving. specification/failures.mdx §Refusal Conditions withdrew the five-condition placement walk; see DECISIONS.md §Typed failures. WHY IT NOW PASSES, and it is the clearest demonstration in the corpus of what the withdrawn rule was actually protecting: `scoreOf("ada")! + scoreOf("bob")!` has TWO propagations, and BOTH hoist, in authored order. The emitted statement calls `scoreOf("ada")`, checks it, calls `scoreOf("bob")`, checks it, and only then adds — which is exactly the authored order, so nothing was reordered by admitting it. The stdout is the proof rather than a formality: `bob` is missing, and the program prints that failure, which can only happen if the second guard ran after the second call and not before the first. Contrast `precededByUnhoistedEffect` in poc/src/language/semantic.ts, which still refuses `g() + r!`: there the left operand leaves an effect the lowering does NOT hoist, so the guard would jump in front of it. Two operands, one operator, opposite verdicts — and the difference is what is to the left, not where the `!` sits.

xfail.reason: the fork still enforces the withdrawn statement-walk and refuses this program with the SMITHERS1204s the retired expectation named. That is a FAIL-CLOSED divergence: the fork compiles nothing and runs nothing, so no marker here holds a fail-open. `safeUnwrapPlacement` in compiler/forkbridge/lowering.go.txt is the fork's copy of the withdrawn walk and has not been widened yet. MEASURED on both backends with `node conformance/runner/run.mjs --filter 02-unwrap-propagation`. The marker retires when the fork's walk is narrowed to the three residual conditions the reference now applies: a conditionally evaluated operand, a repeated loop header, and a propagation preceded by an unhoisted effect in the same statement.
